findings.title: Dereferences possibly undefined first destination calendar
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining. `evt.destinationCalendar` may be null/empty (the destructure yields undefined), so `create()` throws a TypeError for any event with a Google Meet location and no destination calendar, breaking booking creation that previously worked.

findings.title: credentialId for calendar references no longer falls back to the destination calendar
findings.body: The reference's credentialId was previously taken from evt.destinationCalendar.credentialId. Now it is `result.credentialId` only for calendar results, and `externalCalendarId` is `result.externalId`, which is set only by createEvent. Calendar results from the 'other_calendar' path or failed/undefined results can leave references without credentialId/externalCalendarId, so later updates/deletes fall back to the type-based loop and may update every calendar of that type instead of the selected one.

findings.title: Destination calendar entries without credentialId and integration cause unscoped creation
findings.body: In the non-credentialId branch, the filter `c.type === destination.integration` runs when integration is missing or null, matching nothing, but when multiple collective hosts share the same integration type each host's destination calendar triggers createEvent on all credentials of that type. Duplicate events can be created on the same account for collective bookings.

findings.title: Team destination calendars pushed into evt.destinationCalendar for collective events without dedupe
findings.body: `teamDestinationCalendars` is filled from `users.slice(1)` and then appended to `evt.destinationCalendar`. If the organizer's own calendar is already in the array or the same calendar appears twice, the event is created multiple times on the same calendar. Also `evt.destinationCalendar?.push` is a no-op when destinationCalendar is null, silently dropping the team calendars.

findings.title: Booking destinationCalendar connects only the first entry
findings.body: The booking is linked to `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` only, while the collective flow now creates events on several destination calendars. The additional calendars are not recorded on the booking, so they cannot be found later for update or cancel.

findings.title: loadUsers swallows and remaps errors, and changes the hosts-empty fallback
findings.body: The rewritten loadUsers throws a generic HttpError 500 for any unexpected error, hiding the real cause. The dynamic-user branch now throws if the list is empty, where it previously returned an empty list. The hosts branch returns `users.length ? users : eventType.users`, which changes which users are loaded when hosts exist but are empty. These are behavior changes unrelated to the PR's stated purpose.

findings.title: Team member objects gain firstName/lastName and lose nothing, but email fallback changed
findings.body: The teamMemberPromises mapping adds empty firstName/lastName fields and changes `user.email || ""` to `?? ""`, and the comment now says the organizer is not a team member even for non-team events where users.slice(1) may be used. Unrequested changes that risk payload shape differences in emails and webhooks.

findings.title: Lookup compares externalCalendarId against itself, always yielding undefined
findings.body: In updateEvent, the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the comparison is against null/empty and never matches. The selected calendar becomes undefined and the Google update is sent to calendarId undefined. The same bug is in deleteEvent at line 317.

findings.title: Patch call uses selectedCalendar which may be undefined
findings.body: In createEvent, the follow-up patch uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without the `|| "primary"` fallback used in insert, so the patch can target an undefined calendar when no destination matches the credential.

findings.title: createEvent signature drift and new externalId parameter not consumed by calendars
findings.body: createEvent now accepts externalId and passes credential.id to calendar.createEvent, but the Calendar interface and most implementations (Lark, Office365, CalDAV) do not use the per-credential selection. The destination chosen in EventManager is lost for those integrations, so events go to the primary or first calendar.

findings.title: Primary flag computed from the first destination only
findings.body: listCalendars marks primary only for the first destination calendar's externalId, ignoring other collective host destinations, so the UI may mark the wrong calendar as primary.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents now fetches credentials from DB inside a loop without error handling
findings.body: The new credential fallback performs prisma queries per reference and any failure is caught by the outer catch, which returns error results for every reference. A single missing credential now turns a reschedule into failed results for all calendars.

findings.title: Recurring cancel path reuses outer calendar and ignores per-reference credential
findings.body: Inside the recurring branch the inner `calendar` variable shadows the outer one, and the deletion loop for every credential uses `updBooking.references` without matching credentialId. Deletions may target the wrong calendar account for collective bookings.

findings.title: Removed console.error for failed update message
findings.body: The `console.error(message)` call was removed in the catch block of updateAllCalendarEvents, so failures in updating calendar events are silently swallowed with no log.

findings.title: Expected payload changed without a matching behavior assertion
findings.body: The BOOKING_REJECTED expectation now asserts destinationCalendar is an empty array, but the test does not verify the collective multi-host behavior the PR claims to fix, and no unit or e2e test is added for collective destination calendars.
